title: On Short Leave to Japan
omitted_from_reading: The half-title, the printed contents (with the topics of each chapter), the list of illustrations, and the printer’s imprint are in the JSON only.
summary: George John Younghusband (1859–1944), a captain in the Queen’s Own Corps of Guides of the Indian Army, spent a few months’ leave in Japan in 1893 with one companion (the preface speaks of “two young people”). They went by train across India to Calcutta in May, sat out a cyclone below the city, and sailed by way of Penang, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Shanghai to Kobe and Yokohama.

In Japan they stayed in Tokyo, Nikko, Ikao, and Hakone, went along the Tokaido to Lake Biwa and Kyoto, and ended at Osaka and Nara. He writes about hotels and inns, the theatre, temples, shops, and railways, often comparing them with India. The chapters on the voyage say much about the Chinese in the ports, in the language of a British officer of the time. Chapter XVI gives the costs of the journey; the last chapter describes the Japanese army.
notes_on_text: Transcribed from the copy at the University of California (Internet Archive: onshortleavetoja00younrich).

The List of Illustrations places “Tea-House Waitress” facing page 71; in this copy and in the Cornell copy (cu31924023219748) it is bound as the frontispiece, and it is shown there. Four of the plates are printed sideways on the page and are shown upright.
The signboards and the notice that the author copied are set in ruled boxes in the book; here they are centred lines or, for the two signboards side by side on page 41, a table.
